audit_status.source_base: Greek Romans text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for opening, gospel, trust, righteousness/justice, wrath as unveiling, idolatry exchange, degraded patterns. Handle with care; do not weaponize.

verses.restored: Paul, servant of Messiah Jesus, called as apostle, set apart for the good news of the Divine,

familiar.text: Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, called to be an apostle, separated unto the gospel of God,

modern.text: Paul, a servant of Christ Jesus, called to be an apostle, and set apart for the gospel of God—

original.text: Παῦλος δοῦλος ⸂Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ⸃, κλητὸς ἀπόστολος, ἀφωρισμένος εἰς εὐαγγέλιον θεοῦ

verses.restored: which he promised beforehand through his prophets in holy Scriptures,

familiar.text: (Which he had promised afore by his prophets in the holy scriptures,)

modern.text: the gospel He promised beforehand through His prophets in the Holy Scriptures,

original.text: ὃ προεπηγγείλατο διὰ τῶν προφητῶν αὐτοῦ ἐν γραφαῖς ἁγίαις

verses.restored: concerning his Son, who came from the seed of David according to flesh,

familiar.text: Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;

modern.text: regarding His Son, who was a descendant of David according to the flesh,

original.text: περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, τοῦ γενομένου ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα,

verses.restored: and was marked out Son of the Divine in power according to Spirit of holiness by resurrection of the dead: Jesus Messiah our Lord,

familiar.text: And declared to be the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead:

modern.text: and who through the Spirit of holiness was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead: Jesus Christ our Lord.

original.text: τοῦ ὁρισθέντος υἱοῦ θεοῦ ἐν δυνάμει κατὰ πνεῦμα ἁγιωσύνης ἐξ ἀναστάσεως νεκρῶν, Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν,

verses.restored: through whom we received grace and apostleship for obedience of trust among all the nations for his name,

familiar.text: By whom we have received grace and apostleship, for obedience to the faith among all nations, for his name:

modern.text: Through Him and on behalf of His name, we received grace and apostleship to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith.

original.text: διʼ οὗ ἐλάβομεν χάριν καὶ ἀποστολὴν εἰς ὑπακοὴν πίστεως ἐν πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ,

verses.restored: among whom you also are called ones of Jesus Messiah,

familiar.text: Among whom are ye also the called of Jesus Christ:

modern.text: And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ.

original.text: ἐν οἷς ἐστε καὶ ὑμεῖς κλητοὶ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,

verses.restored: to all those in Rome, beloved of the Divine, called holy ones: grace to you and peace from Divine our Father and Lord Jesus Messiah.

familiar.text: To all that be in Rome, beloved of God, called to be saints: Grace to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.

modern.text: To all in Rome who are loved by God and called to be saints: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Unashamed of the Gospel

original.text: πᾶσιν τοῖς οὖσιν ἐν Ῥώμῃ ἀγαπητοῖς θεοῦ, κλητοῖς ἁγίοις· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

verses.restored: First, I thank my Divine through Jesus Messiah for all of you, because your trust is announced in the whole world.

familiar.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your faith is spoken of throughout the whole world.

modern.text: First, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for all of you, because your faith is being proclaimed all over the world.

original.text: Πρῶτον μὲν εὐχαριστῶ τῷ θεῷ μου διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ⸀περὶ πάντων ὑμῶν, ὅτι ἡ πίστις ὑμῶν καταγγέλλεται ἐν ὅλῳ τῷ κόσμῳ.

verses.restored: For the Divine is my witness, whom I serve in my spirit in the good news of his Son, how unceasingly I make mention of you,

familiar.text: For God is my witness, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his Son, that without ceasing I make mention of you always in my prayers;

modern.text: God, whom I serve with my spirit in preaching the gospel of His Son, is my witness how constantly I remember you

original.text: μάρτυς γάρ μού ἐστιν ὁ θεός, ᾧ λατρεύω ἐν τῷ πνεύματί μου ἐν τῷ εὐαγγελίῳ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ, ὡς ἀδιαλείπτως μνείαν ὑμῶν ποιοῦμαι

verses.restored: always in my prayers asking if somehow now at last I may be prospered in the will of the Divine to come to you.

familiar.text: Making request, if by any means now at length I might have a prosperous journey by the will of God to come unto you.

modern.text: in my prayers at all times, asking that now at last by God’s will I may succeed in coming to you.

original.text: πάντοτε ἐπὶ τῶν προσευχῶν μου, δεόμενος εἴ πως ἤδη ποτὲ εὐοδωθήσομαι ἐν τῷ θελήματι τοῦ θεοῦ ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: For I long to see you, so that I may share with you some spiritual gift, to strengthen you,

familiar.text: For I long to see you, that I may impart unto you some spiritual gift, to the end ye may be established;

modern.text: For I long to see you so that I may impart to you some spiritual gift to strengthen you,

original.text: ἐπιποθῶ γὰρ ἰδεῖν ὑμᾶς, ἵνα τι μεταδῶ χάρισμα ὑμῖν πνευματικὸν εἰς τὸ στηριχθῆναι ὑμᾶς,

verses.restored: that is, to be mutually encouraged among you through one another's trust, both yours and mine.

familiar.text: That is, that I may be comforted together with you by the mutual faith both of you and me.

modern.text: that is, that you and I may be mutually encouraged by each other’s faith.

original.text: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν συμπαρακληθῆναι ἐν ὑμῖν διὰ τῆς ἐν ἀλλήλοις πίστεως ὑμῶν τε καὶ ἐμοῦ.

verses.restored: I do not want you to be unaware, siblings, that often I planned to come to you, and was prevented until now, so that I might have some fruit also among you, just as among the rest of the nations.

familiar.text: Now I would not have you ignorant, brethren, that oftentimes I purposed to come unto you, (but was let hitherto,) that I might have some fruit among you also, even as among other Gentiles.

modern.text: I do not want you to be unaware, brothers, how often I planned to come to you (but have been prevented from visiting until now), in order that I might have a harvest among you, just as I have had among the other Gentiles.

original.text: οὐ θέλω δὲ ὑμᾶς ἀγνοεῖν, ἀδελφοί, ὅτι πολλάκις προεθέμην ἐλθεῖν πρὸς ὑμᾶς, καὶ ἐκωλύθην ἄχρι τοῦ δεῦρο, ἵνα τινὰ καρπὸν σχῶ καὶ ἐν ὑμῖν καθὼς καὶ ἐν τοῖς λοιποῖς ἔθνεσιν.

verses.restored: I am debtor both to Greeks and to non-Greeks, both to wise and to uncomprehending.

familiar.text: I am debtor both to the Greeks, and to the Barbarians; both to the wise, and to the unwise.

modern.text: I am obligated both to Greeks and non-Greeks, both to the wise and the foolish.

original.text: Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, σοφοῖς τε καὶ ἀνοήτοις ὀφειλέτης εἰμί·

verses.restored: Thus, for my part, I am eager to announce the good news also to you who are in Rome.

familiar.text: So, as much as in me is, I am ready to preach the gospel to you that are at Rome also.

modern.text: That is why I am so eager to preach the gospel also to you who are in Rome.

original.text: οὕτως τὸ κατʼ ἐμὲ πρόθυμον καὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς ἐν Ῥώμῃ εὐαγγελίσασθαι.

verses.restored: For I am not ashamed of the good news; for it is power of the Divine for salvation/healing to everyone trusting, to Judean first and also to Greek.

familiar.text: For I am not ashamed of the gospel of Christ: for it is the power of God unto salvation to every one that believeth; to the Jew first, and also to the Greek.

modern.text: I am not ashamed of the gospel, because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, first to the Jew, then to the Greek.

original.text: Οὐ γὰρ ἐπαισχύνομαι τὸ ⸀εὐαγγέλιον, δύναμις γὰρ θεοῦ ἐστιν εἰς σωτηρίαν παντὶ τῷ πιστεύοντι, Ἰουδαίῳ τε πρῶτον καὶ Ἕλληνι·

verses.restored: For in it the righteousness/justice of the Divine is unveiled from trust into trust, just as it is written: The righteous/just one will live from trust.

familiar.text: For therein is the righteousness of God revealed from faith to faith: as it is written, The just shall live by faith.

modern.text: For the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish, just as it is written: “The righteous will live by faith.” God’s Wrath against Sin

original.text: δικαιοσύνη γὰρ θεοῦ ἐν αὐτῷ ἀποκαλύπτεται ἐκ πίστεως εἰς πίστιν, καθὼς γέγραπται· Ὁ δὲ δίκαιος ἐκ πίστεως ζήσεται.

verses.restored: For wrath of the Divine is unveiled from heaven against all ungodliness and injustice of humans who hold down the truth in injustice,

familiar.text: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men, who hold the truth in unrighteousness;

modern.text: The wrath of God is being revealed from heaven against all the godlessness and wickedness of men who suppress the truth by their wickedness.

original.text: Ἀποκαλύπτεται γὰρ ὀργὴ θεοῦ ἀπʼ οὐρανοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσαν ἀσέβειαν καὶ ἀδικίαν ἀνθρώπων τῶν τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐν ἀδικίᾳ κατεχόντων,

verses.restored: because what is knowable of the Divine is manifest among them, for the Divine made it manifest to them.

familiar.text: Because that which may be known of God is manifest in them; for God hath shewed it unto them.

modern.text: For what may be known about God is plain to them, because God has made it plain to them.

original.text: διότι τὸ γνωστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ φανερόν ἐστιν ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ ⸂θεὸς γὰρ⸃ αὐτοῖς ἐφανέρωσεν.

verses.restored: For the unseen things of him, both his everlasting power and divine nature, being understood from the created order, are perceived through what has been made, so that they are without excuse.

familiar.text: For the invisible things of him from the creation of the world are clearly seen, being understood by the things that are made, even his eternal power and Godhead; so that they are without excuse:

modern.text: For since the creation of the world God’s invisible qualities, His eternal power and divine nature, have been clearly seen, being understood from His workmanship, so that men are without excuse.

original.text: τὰ γὰρ ἀόρατα αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ κτίσεως κόσμου τοῖς ποιήμασιν νοούμενα καθορᾶται, ἥ τε ἀΐδιος αὐτοῦ δύναμις καὶ θειότης, εἰς τὸ εἶναι αὐτοὺς ἀναπολογήτους,

verses.restored: Because knowing the Divine, they did not glorify as Divine or give thanks, but became empty in their reasonings, and their uncomprehending heart was darkened.

familiar.text: Because that, when they knew God, they glorified him not as God, neither were thankful; but became vain in their imaginations, and their foolish heart was darkened.

modern.text: For although they knew God, they neither glorified Him as God nor gave thanks to Him, but they became futile in their thinking and darkened in their foolish hearts.

original.text: διότι γνόντες τὸν θεὸν οὐχ ὡς θεὸν ἐδόξασαν ἢ ηὐχαρίστησαν, ἀλλὰ ἐματαιώθησαν ἐν τοῖς διαλογισμοῖς αὐτῶν καὶ ἐσκοτίσθη ἡ ἀσύνετος αὐτῶν καρδία·

verses.restored: Claiming to be wise, they became foolish,

familiar.text: Professing themselves to be wise, they became fools,

modern.text: Although they claimed to be wise, they became fools,

original.text: φάσκοντες εἶναι σοφοὶ ἐμωράνθησαν,

verses.restored: and exchanged the glory of the imperishable Divine for a likeness of an image of perishable human and birds and four-footed creatures and reptiles.

familiar.text: And changed the glory of the uncorruptible God into an image made like to corruptible man, and to birds, and fourfooted beasts, and creeping things.

modern.text: and exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of mortal man and birds and animals and reptiles.

original.text: καὶ ἤλλαξαν τὴν δόξαν τοῦ ἀφθάρτου θεοῦ ἐν ὁμοιώματι εἰκόνος φθαρτοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πετεινῶν καὶ τετραπόδων καὶ ἑρπετῶν.

verses.restored: Therefore the Divine handed them over in the desires of their hearts to uncleanness, to dishonor their bodies among themselves,

familiar.text: Wherefore God also gave them up to uncleanness through the lusts of their own hearts, to dishonour their own bodies between themselves:

modern.text: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity for the dishonoring of their bodies with one another.

original.text: ⸀Διὸ παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς ἐν ταῖς ἐπιθυμίαις τῶν καρδιῶν αὐτῶν εἰς ἀκαθαρσίαν τοῦ ἀτιμάζεσθαι τὰ σώματα αὐτῶν ἐν ⸀αὐτοῖς,

verses.restored: they who exchanged the truth of the Divine for the lie, and revered and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed into the ages. Amen.

familiar.text: Who changed the truth of God into a lie, and worshipped and served the creature more than the Creator, who is blessed for ever. Amen.

modern.text: They exchanged the truth of God for a lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is forever worthy of praise! Amen.

original.text: οἵτινες μετήλλαξαν τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐν τῷ ψεύδει, καὶ ἐσεβάσθησαν καὶ ἐλάτρευσαν τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα, ὅς ἐστιν εὐλογητὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας· ἀμήν.

verses.restored: Because of this the Divine handed them over to dishonorable passions; for their females exchanged natural use for what is beyond/against nature,

familiar.text: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:

modern.text: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.

original.text: Διὰ τοῦτο παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς πάθη ἀτιμίας· αἵ τε γὰρ θήλειαι αὐτῶν μετήλλαξαν τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν εἰς τὴν παρὰ φύσιν,

verses.restored: and likewise also the males, leaving natural use of the female, were inflamed in their desire for one another, males with males working what is shameful and receiving in themselves the return that was fitting for their error.

familiar.text: And likewise also the men, leaving the natural use of the woman, burned in their lust one toward another; men with men working that which is unseemly, and receiving in themselves that recompence of their error which was meet.

modern.text: Likewise, the men abandoned natural relations with women and burned with lust for one another. Men committed indecent acts with other men, and received in themselves the due penalty for their error.

original.text: ὁμοίως τε καὶ οἱ ἄρσενες ἀφέντες τὴν φυσικὴν χρῆσιν τῆς θηλείας ἐξεκαύθησαν ἐν τῇ ὀρέξει αὐτῶν εἰς ἀλλήλους, ἄρσενες ἐν ἄρσεσιν τὴν ἀσχημοσύνην κατεργαζόμενοι καὶ τὴν ἀντιμισθίαν ἣν ἔδει τῆς πλάνης αὐτῶν ἐν ⸀ἑαυτοῖς ἀπολαμβάνοντες.

verses.restored: And just as they did not approve to hold the Divine in knowledge, the Divine handed them over to an unapproved mind, to do things not fitting,

familiar.text: And even as they did not like to retain God in their knowledge, God gave them over to a reprobate mind, to do those things which are not convenient;

modern.text: Furthermore, since they did not see fit to acknowledge God, He gave them up to a depraved mind, to do what ought not to be done.

original.text: Καὶ καθὼς οὐκ ἐδοκίμασαν τὸν θεὸν ἔχειν ἐν ἐπιγνώσει, παρέδωκεν αὐτοὺς ὁ θεὸς εἰς ἀδόκιμον νοῦν, ποιεῖν τὰ μὴ καθήκοντα,

verses.restored: having been filled with every injustice, wickedness, greed, malice; full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, harmful character; whisperers,

familiar.text: Being filled with all unrighteousness, fornication, wickedness, covetousness, maliciousness; full of envy, murder, debate, deceit, malignity; whisperers,

modern.text: They have become filled with every kind of wickedness, evil, greed, and depravity. They are full of envy, murder, strife, deceit, and malice. They are gossips,

original.text: πεπληρωμένους πάσῃ ⸀ἀδικίᾳ πονηρίᾳ πλεονεξίᾳ κακίᾳ, μεστοὺς φθόνου φόνου ἔριδος δόλου κακοηθείας, ψιθυριστάς,

verses.restored: slanderers, Divine-haters, insolent, arrogant, boastful, inventors of harmful things, disobedient to parents,

familiar.text: Backbiters, haters of God, despiteful, proud, boasters, inventors of evil things, disobedient to parents,

modern.text: slanderers, God-haters, insolent, arrogant, and boastful. They invent new forms of evil; they disobey their parents.

original.text: καταλάλους, θεοστυγεῖς, ὑβριστάς, ὑπερηφάνους, ἀλαζόνας, ἐφευρετὰς κακῶν, γονεῦσιν ἀπειθεῖς,

verses.restored: without understanding, covenant-breaking, without natural affection, without mercy.

familiar.text: Without understanding, covenantbreakers, without natural affection, implacable, unmerciful:

modern.text: They are senseless, faithless, heartless, merciless.

original.text: ἀσυνέτους, ἀσυνθέτους, ⸀ἀστόργους, ἀνελεήμονας·

verses.restored: These, knowing the righteous/just decree of the Divine, that those practicing such things are worthy of death, not only do them but also approve those practicing them.

familiar.text: Who knowing the judgment of God, that they which commit such things are worthy of death, not only do the same, but have pleasure in them that do them.

modern.text: Although they know God’s righteous decree that those who do such things are worthy of death, they not only continue to do these things, but also approve of those who practice them.

original.text: οἵτινες τὸ δικαίωμα τοῦ θεοῦ ἐπιγνόντες, ὅτι οἱ τὰ τοιαῦτα πράσσοντες ἄξιοι θανάτου εἰσίν, οὐ μόνον αὐτὰ ποιοῦσιν ἀλλὰ καὶ συνευδοκοῦσιν τοῖς πράσσουσιν.

safety_note: Romans 1 is presented as part of Paul's wider indictment of idolatrous exchange and distorted desire leading into Romans 2-3, where Paul turns the critique on the judging reader and establishes universal accountability. This draft should not be detached as a weapon against sexual minorities or used to flatten Paul's argument into anti-LGBT rhetoric.
